experience.title: Incoming Nanofabrication Engineer
bullets: Incoming nanofabrication internship in UMass Lowell's shared cleanroom and characterization facilities.

experience.title: Process Engineer
bullets: Optimized bottom-up Cu electroplating of 20 × 200 µm high-aspect-ratio features through DOE-driven variation of bath chemistry, temperature, dwell time, vacuum prewet and current-density waveforms, cutting customer wafer fill time by 50%, from a 10-hour benchmark to 5 hours.

Developed wafer-level electrochemical deposition (ECD) and metallization processes for Cu, In and Pd across TSV, TGV, damascene and advanced-packaging structures to improve throughput and process efficiency.

Performed process and hardware qualification using optical profilometry, AOI, X-ray imaging, cross-sectional analysis and defect analysis to characterize panel-level plating performance across process conditions and hardware configurations.

Analyzed Cu thickness, roughness, uniformity, terminal effects, feature fill and overburden in JMP and Excel, turning metrology data into recommendations that supported process optimization and qualification decisions.

Operated, maintained and troubleshot automated ECD and wet-process equipment (process cells, chemical reservoirs, vacuum, fluid-delivery and wafer-handling systems, electrical interfaces, CDA/N₂ utilities), diagnosing faults through root-cause analysis to sustain repeatable plating and equipment uptime.

experience.title: Research Associate, Ultra-Wide Bandgap Semiconductors
experience.org: Bhuiyan Research Group · PI: Dr. Anhar Bhuiyan
bullets: Supported LPCVD growth of gallium oxide (Ga₂O₃) thin films through substrate preparation, wafer cleaving, precursor handling, reactor setup, gas-flow calibration and process monitoring.
Maintained detailed experimental documentation across growth runs to support reproducible deposition, controlled thin-film growth and run-to-run repeatability.
Characterized Ga₂O₃ films with XRD, SEM, AFM and Hall effect measurements to evaluate crystal structure, surface morphology, film quality and electrical properties.
Correlated characterization results with LPCVD growth parameters through literature review and data analysis, contributing to growth-parameter optimization for a Ga₂O₃ epitaxial growth project.
Presented findings at a university research symposium and in the 3-Minute Thesis (3MT) competition.

experience.title: Research Associate, Photonics
experience.org: Wang Laboratory of Optics · PI: Dr. Xingwei Wang
bullets: Fabricated fiber-optic biosensors, strain sensors and shape sensors in the cleanroom through fiber splicing, stripping, shaping and chemical etching (glass etchant, BOE, HCl-based solutions).
Developed a fiber-optic glucose biosensor as a key project: reviewed state-of-the-art glucose-sensing methods, then designed an approach tailored to the lab's objectives and constraints.
Engineered an alternative fiber-shaping technique to replace the lab's tapered-edge process, and validated it through extensive testing and data analysis.
Characterized spectral response, wavelength shifts and signal stability using optical frequency domain reflectometry (OFDR) on an ODiSI system.
Coordinated with domestic and international vendors to source optical components, managed lab inventory and orders, and kept the lab's Tridion-based website up to date.

work.title: AI/ML Model Validation Fellow
bullets: Validated, annotated and quality-audited multimodal datasets used in supervised learning and model fine-tuning.
Evaluated model outputs to identify failure modes, edge cases and distribution shifts, informing improvements in accuracy and bias reduction.

Led a digital branding and social media initiative, creating the content strategy and all visual assets, and grew the office's social presence by 40% with over 60,000 impressions.

projects.title: ARM Assembly Blackjack System
projects.text: An ARM-based embedded blackjack game with real-time game logic, memory management and modular subroutines written in ARM Assembly. It drives a 20×4 I²C LCD and GPIO controls, with 3.3 V / 5 V level-shifting circuitry, debugged across both hardware and software. (The blackjack table on the street runs the same rules.)

projects.title: Colpitts Oscillator
projects.text: An LM741-based Colpitts oscillator using LC resonance and diode feedback stabilization. Component values were iterated in LTspice to reach a 7 kHz sinusoidal output, then frequency response, waveform stability and harmonic performance were validated with FFT analysis.

projects.title: Telephone Dialing Simulation
projects.text: A software touch-tone telephone that maps each dialed digit to its DTMF frequency pair, then synthesizes and concatenates the waveforms to play phone numbers, ringing tones and busy signals.

projects.title: Traffic Light Controller
projects.text: An Arduino traffic light for a dual-direction intersection, built on a breadboard with LEDs, digital I/O and push-button inputs, with timing logic that coordinates green, yellow and red cycles like a real crossing.

about.lede: I'm R.J., a Computer Engineering student at UMass Lowell who wears a lot of hats. Most of them end up being cleanroom hoods.
paragraphs: My specialty is semiconductors. At Applied Materials I developed copper electroplating for high-aspect-ratio features and cut a customer's wafer fill time in half. Before that I grew Ga₂O₃ thin films by LPCVD in the Bhuiyan Research Group and built fiber-optic sensors in the Wang Laboratory of Optics. Next I'm joining UMass Lowell's Core Research Facilities as a nanofabrication engineering intern.

Outside the lab I founded and lead IGNITE, mentor first-generation engineering students, and I'm a Shah Academy Scholar; the SK Youth Center down the street has the full list. This site is the rest of me: a barangay street, a basketball court, and a brown Mazda6 with a CHOIKI plate.
